flags: vcut = -0.1 is a negative value. EXCLURAD branches on the sign of vcut: negative values switch the code from the ordinary missing-mass-squared cut to a different ('v'-type) inelasticity interpretation, per the input-file comment. This is not physically impossible and the preflight check returned only a WARN (not FAIL), so the point and vcut as given were used verbatim -- but a negative vcut is an unusual choice and may not be what was intended if a plain 0.1 GeV^2 cut was meant.

Beam energy defaulted to 6.53 GeV (CLAS12 RG-K campaign, the validated eta reference energy). Alternatives (10.6 GeV RG-A, 10.2 GeV RG-B) would give different radiative corrections; state the beam energy used when reporting results.
rc_mode defaulted to 'full' (O(alpha) calculation), consistent with the validated eta results.
explanation: The kinematic point W=1.7 GeV, Q2=1.0 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0, phi=90 deg passed every physical check (production threshold, pole safety, Q2 positivity, beam accessibility, lookup-table coverage, phi range) with no issues. The only anomaly is vcut=-0.1: EXCLURAD treats a negative vcut as a request for a different cut interpretation ('v' mode) rather than as an error, so the request is not physically impossible and was honored as given. Because this could easily be an unintended sign (e.g. the user meant a 0.1 GeV^2 cut), I generated the input file with vcut=-0.1 exactly as requested but flagged the sign-dependent behavior explicitly rather than silently normalizing it to 0.1, so the physicist can confirm intent before running EXCLURAD.
